Row.Text: The Viet people rule over a wide array of peoples: terraced rice fields and shaded taro gardens in the highlands, low rice fields green with grain. But wherever administrators go, they see room for improvement – canals, reservoirs, roads, and the like. Each one brings more yield; each one brings more administration; each one brings more tax revenue.
Take time. Implement reforms. Make the land yield what it can yield.

The Đại Việt foreign ministry is a hub of activity. Vietnamese-style hangings are switched out, tables and chairs are brought in, and in a flash all of the courtiers change from Vietnamese dress to foreign - only blackened teeth remain of Đại Việt fashion. This is not capitulation, but strategy: foreigners come to negotiate, and Đại Việt shows that they understand foreign games.
But the binding deal will be the one in Vietnamese.
And the binding deal will be the one in an international tongue.
